fixes.explanation: True, baker. Numbers 33:4 says the Egyptians were burying all their firstborn, "…whom the LORD had struck down among them…" Then the verse adds one more thing: "for the LORD had executed judgment against their gods." So the striking down and the judgment against their gods are both right there in that one verse.

Mount Carmel isn't one of the stops in this list. Numbers 33:37 says that after Kadesh they camped at Mount Hor, "…on the outskirts of the land of Edom." Forty-some camp names in a row and I'm already squinting. I read that list once and my brain said, "Papa, just bake something." Mount Hor is the one, friend.

That's it, baker! Numbers 33:40 says the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, "…heard that the Israelites were coming." A whole nation on the move, and the word gets around. The verse stops right there and doesn't tell us what he did with the news. I'd have checked my front door twice.

Egypt's army? Friend, Egypt is way back in the rearview mirror by this point. Numbers 33:40 says the Canaanite king of Arad "…heard that the Israelites were coming." The news is about Israel on the move, and Egypt's army isn't in this verse at all. That one sounds like a rerun, and this is a whole new episode.
